compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Per-expert GEMMs are MxK=1024, NxK with intermediate=2816. With N=1024 tokens, top_k=2 => 2048 routed slots, ~256 per expert avg. M is small-ish; tensor cores want M>=16. FP16 with FP32 accum -> 210 TFLOPS peak.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Bulk of FLOPs are in three GEMMs per expert: gate(MxKxN), up(MxKxN), down(MxNxK). Total ~ 2 * 1024 * 2 * (1024*2816*2 + 2816*1024) FLOPs ~ a few GFLOPs; bandwidth-bound likely due to small M.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Tensor-core utilization low if M per expert is small or uneven.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Expert weights total ~ 8 * (2816*1024*2 + 1024*2816) * 2B = ~135 MB. Larger than L2 (64MB). Each expert's weights ~17 MB — fit partially in L2. Reading weights once per token group is key.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Weight reload per expert dominates if M is small.

register_pressure.notes: Standard GEMM tiles (e.g., BM=64, BN=128, BK=32) within bounds.

nodes.notes:
PROBLEM: Mixtral-style MoE forward. Components: (1) gate linear (1024->8) + softmax + topk(2) + normalize, (2) permute by expert via argsort, (3) per-expert SwiGLU FFN (gate_proj 1024->2816, up_proj 1024->2816, silu*mul, down_proj 2816->1024), (4) scatter-add weighted outputs.
INPUT: (2,512,1024) fp16 => N=1024 tokens, 2048 routed slots, ~256/expert avg.
LAYOUT: w1,w3: (E,I,D) row-major; w2: (E,D,I). All fp16.
BOTTLENECKS: Per-expert GEMMs dominate; small M per expert -> low TC utilization; many kernel launches in eager loop hurts.
REGIMES: (a) balanced routing M~256/expert => GEMM bandwidth-bound on weights; (b) imbalanced => some experts large -> compute, others tiny -> launch overhead; (c) gating itself is tiny (1024x1024x8) negligible.
KNOBS: grouped GEMM kernel (single kernel over all experts using offsets), fused gate+up+silu in one kernel writing intermediate (M,I), then down_proj kernel that fuses scatter-add with weighting. Use tl.dot with FP32 accum.
FUSION: gate_proj + up_proj + silu*mul can fuse (share input load of x). down_proj can fuse with weight multiplication and scatter_add (atomic add to original token slots, multiplied by topk weight) — eliminates expert_outputs buffer.
SKELETON: kernel1: gating+softmax+topk+normalize+build permutation via sort on CPU/GPU (use torch.argsort). kernel2: fused gate+up+silu producing intermediate[2048, 2816]. kernel3: down_proj + weight + atomic scatter_add into output[1024,1024].
ALT: gather input via permuted indices inside kernel2 (avoid materializing permuted_tokens).
OPEN ACTIONS: (A) grouped-GEMM fused gate/up/silu reading x via gather, (B) down_proj fused with weighted scatter_add, (C) fused gating+topk+norm kernel.

action.description: Implement a Triton grouped-GEMM kernel that, for each expert, computes intermediate = SiLU(x @ W1^T) * (x @ W3^T) over the tokens assigned to that expert. Use expert offsets (cumulative counts) so a single launch handles all experts. Gather x rows via sorted_token_ids inside the kernel (no permuted_tokens materialization). Tile (BM, BN, BK) sized for tensor cores; accumulate in FP32.
action.rationale: Eliminates 7 separate kernel launches per expert (the Python loop) and removes a separate up_proj pass + intermediate materialization of permuted_tokens. Reads x once per output tile.

kernel_summary: Mixtral-style MoE forward: gate linear + softmax + top-k(2) + normalize, sort tokens by expert, per-expert SwiGLU FFN (gate_proj 1024->2816, up_proj, SiLU*mul, down_proj 2816->1024), weighted scatter-add. With (B,S,D)=(2,512,1024), top_k=2, E=8: 2048 routed slots, ~256 tokens/expert. Bulk of work is three GEMMs per expert; small M makes tensor-core utilization sensitive to tiling; the Python per-expert loop adds 7×3 = ~24 small kernel launches. Strategy: (1) fused gating kernel; (2) grouped fused gate+up+SiLU kernel using cumulative expert offsets and in-kernel gather of x; (3) fused down_proj + topk weighting + atomic scatter-add into output. FP16 inputs with FP32 accumulators for tensor cores (m16n8k16). Weights (~135 MB) exceed L2 (64 MB) — stream weights once per expert tile and reuse via shared memory tiles.
open_questions: Does Triton on Blackwell sm_100 support atomic_add on fp16? If not, use fp32 output buffer and cast at the end.
What is the actual routing distribution at runtime (balanced vs skewed)? Affects whether per-expert tile counts vary wildly.
Optimal tile shape (BM, BN, BK) for M~32-64 per expert tile and N=2816 on RTX 5090 (Blackwell)?
Is materializing permuted_tokens cheaper than gathering x rows inside the GEMM kernel (cache reuse vs extra pass)?
Stable argsort: can we replace with a bucket-count + prefix-sum kernel cheaper than torch.argsort for E=8?
Does torch.compile already fuse the per-expert loop? If so the bar is higher; need to compare against compiled baseline.
Can we avoid sorting entirely by using an unsorted scatter with masks per expert (8 small GEMMs in parallel via grouped GEMM with offsets)?
What's the kernel-launch overhead share vs compute for the chosen tiling — measure to decide fusion priority.
